answer_raw:
I cannot see the response you are referring to, so I cannot judge its quality. My previous answer was thin because it didn't fully explore the scale of the hardware or the specific relationship between the companies involved.

The most powerful specialized AI hardware currently being used for large-scale training is the **Google Trillium TPU** (as of s2024-12-11) [2].

**Claude** is powered by these **TPU clusters** through a massive deal with Google that provides up to **1 million specialized AI chips** to Anthropic (as of 2025-10-25) [1]. This partnership is worth tens of billions of dollars and ensures Anthropic has the compute needed to scale future Claude models [1].

Other major players and their hardware include:
- **Google** used **Trillium TPUs** to train its own **Gemini 2.0** model (as of 2024-12-11) [2].
- **AI21** uses **TPUs** to run their **Mamba** and **Jamba** language models (as of 2024-12-11) [2].
- **NVIDIA** remains a dominant force in the broader market; for instance, the **Tesla V100** (undated) is a well-known data center GPU used for scaling AI inference and training [3].
- **Gemma 3** (as of 2025-03-12) is positioned as the most powerful model you can run on a **single GPU** (as of 2025-03-12) [5].

messages.content: What is the most powerful GPU in the world right now, or TPU, or anything being used for AI? What is Claude using, and what are others using?

The most powerful specialized AI hardware currently being deployed at scale is the **Google Trillium TPU** (as of 2024-12-11) [2].

**Claude** is using Google's **TPU clusters** through a deal worth tens of billions of dollars to power future models [1].

As for other users:
- **Google** used **Trillium TPUs** to train the **Gemini 2.0** model (as of 2024-12-11) [2].
- **AI21** uses **TPUs** for their **Mamba** and **Jamba** language models (as of 2024-12-11) [2].
- The **NVIDIA Tesla V100** is an older data center GPU used for AI training and inferencing (undated) [3].
- **Gemma 3** is described as a model designed to be the most powerful one you can run on a **single GPU** (as of 2025-03-12) [5].
